pairs.why: A's locomotive has soft graded value inside the dark body and a saturated sky gradient like the real cards, while B's black body is flatter and sits in a hazier, paler desert.
A has the real cards' strong value separation of dark orange posts against saturated mid-blue water and sky, while B's pale washed water flattens the whole card toward high key.
B's darker warm wall that falls off toward the top matches the real card's dim, vignetted wall and gives the white cap more separation, while A's bright, even background is too high-key.
A keeps the real card's muted mid-dark navy anchor against a warm background that darkens toward the edges, while B is a bright glossy electric blue with a hot glow behind it.
A's darker hero stands apart from the orange background by both value and hue as the real heroes do, while B's pale teal box sinks into a dull grey floor.
Both cards have a similar key, a similar green hero against warm gradient, and a similar floor, so value gives no clear reason to choose.
B's calculator keeps the real card's dark navy body and keys as one dark mass against bright yellow, whereas A breaks it up with cream keys and a pale glow.
B's saturated pink background and mid-dark purple floor separate the light helmet strongly, as the real cards' saturated backgrounds do, while A's pale lavender background leaves low contrast.
